description: A formal theory: the vocabulary, semantics, and proof environment that requirements are written in. Published by the regulator. A theory record is what makes a requirement mean something to a machine, and it is the object that pins the trusted computing base — toolchain, source digest, and the decoder that turns network records into values the theory can talk about.

version.description: Semver of the theory itself, independent of the record CID. The CID is what proofs bind to; this is for humans.

toolchain.description: Exact proof assistant release, e.g. 'leanprover/lean4:v4.33.1'. A checker that cannot honour this string must refuse to issue a verdict rather than substitute a nearby version.

rootModule.description: Lean module that re-exports the whole theory, e.g. 'Redistrict'.

source.description: The theory's Lean package. Shipped in-band so that verification has no dependency on a package registry staying up or staying honest.

sourceDigest.description: sha256 of the source blob, hex. Redundant with the blob CID by design: it is the value a human quotes and a third-party checker re-derives.

artifactTypes.description: The bridge between the network and the theory. Without this, a proof is about a value someone typed rather than about a record anyone can fetch.

vocabulary.description: Self-description: which phrases the DSL accepts and what each one denotes. Lets a reader who will never run Lean audit what a requirement is claiming.

artifactBinding.description: Declares that records of a given lexicon decode into a given type in the theory, by way of a named total decoder. All three must be stated: the lexicon alone does not fix a representation, and the Lean type alone does not fix which records are eligible.

leanType.description: Fully-qualified type in the theory, e.g. 'Redistrict.Plan'.

decoder.description: Fully-qualified decoder, e.g. 'Redistrict.Codec.decodePlan'. Must be total and canonical: the same record bytes must always yield the same value, or proofs stop being about anything in particular.

phrase.description: The DSL surface syntax, e.g. 'efficiency gap of'.
